Ahhh okay okay 😅 I see what you’re pointing at.

You’re asking:

**In NIRF 2025 Engineering ranking, is Kalasalingam actually ranked above *some* IITs?**

Short answer:  
👉 **Yes — it can appear above a few *newer IITs* in the ranking list.**  
👉 But that does *not* mean it is “better than IITs” overall.

Let’s break it properly.

---

## 🎓 The College You’re Referring To

**entity["organization","Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education","deemed university krishnankoil tamil nadu"]**  
Location: Krishnankoil (near Srivilliputhur), Tamil Nadu  
Type: Deemed-to-be University (Private)

It participates in NIRF Engineering rankings.

---

## 🏆 Why It May Appear Above Some IITs

Not all IITs are the same.

There are:

- Older IITs → like **entity["organization","IIT Madras","indian institute of technology chennai"]** (Top tier, heavy research, strong brand)
- New-generation IITs → like **entity["organization","IIT Bhilai","indian institute of technology chhattisgarh"]**, IIT Dharwad, IIT Jammu, etc.

New IITs:
- Started recently
- Smaller campus
- Fewer PhD faculty
- Lower research volume
- Still building reputation

NIRF ranking is based on:
- Teaching quality
- Research output
- Graduation outcomes
- Perception score
- Inclusivity

So if a newer IIT is still developing infrastructure and research volume, a well-established private university like Kalasalingam **can score higher in some metrics**.

That’s how it may rank above *a few* newer IITs.

---

## ⚠️ But Here’s the Important Reality

Being ranked above a newer IIT in NIRF does NOT mean:

- It has stronger brand value
- It has better industry perception
- It has stronger alumni network
- It has higher global recognition

Older IITs dominate perception + research + placements.

New IITs still carry the “IIT” brand weight.

Rank ≠ brand power.

---

## 🧠 Simple Analogy

Think of it like this:

- Old IIT = Established Premier League club
- New IIT = Young club building legacy
- Kalasalingam = Strong regional team with good stats

Stats can move. Brand legacy takes decades.

---

## 🎯 So Is It “Better Than IIT”?

Depends on what you mean by “better”:

| If you mean | Answer |
|-------------|--------|
| NIRF score in one year | Possibly yes (above some newer IITs) |
| Brand value | No |
| Global recognition | No |
| Research ecosystem | Mostly no (compared to older IITs) |
| Placement power | IITs stronger overall |

---

Now tell me honestly —  
Are you checking this because of:

- Admission decision?
- Domicile / Karnataka discussion?
- Or just ranking curiosity?

Say clearly what you’re evaluating — I’ll break it without confusion.

Here’s what’s going on with the page you shared:  
The link **https://www.nirfindia.org/Rankings/2025/CollegeRanking.html** is **the *College* category of NIRF 2025 rankings — not the *Engineering* rankings**. citeturn0search11

### 📌 What this means
The **NIRF (National Institutional Ranking Framework)** publishes multiple separate ranking lists each year for different kinds of higher-education institutions in India. These include categories such as:  
• **Overall**  
• **Universities**  
• **Colleges**  
• **Engineering**  
• **Management**  
• **Medical**  
• **Law**  
• **Pharmacy**  
…and others. citeturn0search11

So the **“College” ranking page** (which you opened) lists arts, science, commerce, and general degree colleges — e.g., Hindu College, Miranda House, Hans Raj College, St Xavier’s, etc. — **not engineering colleges**. citeturn0view0

### 🎯 Why you see “no engineering colleges”
• The *College* ranking page is specific to that category. Engineering institutes have their own separate ranking page (e.g., *EngineeringRanking.html*). citeturn0search0  
• That’s why you don’t see engineering colleges listed on the *College* page — they belong to a different category within NIRF.  
• In other words: **It’s not that there are zero engineering colleges in NIRF 2025 — they’re just not shown on this page because it’s a different category.**

### 🧭 Where to find the engineering list
For the 2025 *Engineering* rankings, the correct page is:  
➡ **https://www.nirfindia.org/Rankings/2025/EngineeringRanking.html** — which does list engineering colleges like IITs, NITs, etc. citeturn0search0

Here’s what’s going on with your question:

### 📌 1. The institute you mentioned
The institution you’re talking about is **Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education** in Krishnankoil (often shortened to Kalasalingam University). It **is a real institution** in Tamil Nadu that participates in Indian rankings. citeturn0search4

### 📌 2. Where it stands in NIRF 2025
In the **NIRF 2025 Engineering ranking**, the official *top-100 list* (which ranks the best engineering institutions nationwide) is dominated by **Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs)**, National Institutes of Technology (NITs), IIITs, and some well-known private universities like BITS Pilani, etc. citeturn0search12turn0search21  
Institutes like:
- IIT Madras  
- IIT Delhi  
- IIT Bombay  
- IIT Kanpur  
- NIT Trichy  
…are at the top. citeturn0search12

According to lists circulating online (verified by various educational sites), **Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education isn’t in the official top 50 for Engineering in NIRF 2025** — it appears further down the overall engineering ranking *and not among the top-ranked technical institutions*. citeturn0search12turn0search21

It **does appear in broader participation lists** when you download the full alphabetical participation list of all engineering colleges — but that list includes *every college that participated*, not just those in the *ranked top-100*. citeturn0search1

### 📌 3. Why it might *seem* “better” than some IITs
If you saw Kalasalingam above some IITs on *some lists*, here are the possible reasons:

**a) Different ranking metrics/category**  
Some websites show **overall university rankings**, or specific categories like *Innovation ranking*, *Overall category*, etc., which are different from the pure *Engineering ranking*. An institute can do well in one sub-category without being top overall. citeturn0search13

**b) Data mix-ups**  
There are multiple ranking systems in India (NIRF, IIRF, Times HE, etc.). If a page doesn’t clearly state *NIRF Engineering 2025*, it might be mixing data from another ranking system. citeturn0search7

**c) Misinterpretation of list bands**  
NIRF sometimes shows **rank bands** (like 101–150, 151–200) for many colleges. If Kalasalingam appears in a broader list, it doesn’t imply it outranked a top IIT — it just means it participated and got a numeric band or placement. citeturn0search1

### 📌 4. Bottom line
🔥 **No — Kalasalingam Academy of Research and Education is not ranked higher than premier IITs in the official NIRF 2025 Engineering rankings.**  
The top positions are held by IITs and other top-tier national institutes, based on strict criteria like teaching quality, research output, placements, and perception. citeturn0search12

But:
✔ It *does* participate in NIRF. citeturn0search1  
✔ It may show up in ranking bands or other categories. citeturn0search13  
✔ Rankings aren’t the only measure — different students value different aspects (courses, cost, location, specialization, etc.).

## 2️⃣ Why Would an IIT Rank Below Kalasalingam?

NIRF uses 5 weighted metrics:

| Metric | Weight |
|--------|--------|
| Teaching, Learning & Resources | 30% |
| Research & Professional Practice | 30% |
| Graduation Outcomes | 20% |
| Outreach & Inclusivity | 10% |
| Perception | 10% |

New IITs:

- Lower research publications

- Has slightly lower research output
- Fewer PhD publications
- Lower faculty-student ratio

It may lose points there.

Meanwhile, Kalasalingam may score higher in:
- Research count
- Inclusivity
- Faculty strength

So total score changes.

It cares about weighted academic data.
